disagreements.researcher_position: Rule 31(29) and section 4A carry no amendment events relevant to the matter, so both temporal notes say the provisions were untouched.
disagreements.verifier_position: Rule 31(29) was amended by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3(9) (Form F to Form F 1), and section 4A was inserted by Notaries (Amendment) Law No. 20 of 1976 s.4. Neither changes the April 2020 position of the words actually relied on, but the notes as written overstate the position, and the first corpus_gaps entry repeats the rule (29) error.

disagreements.researcher_position: Rule 31(22) bars Nimal Perera from attesting the father's execution in Kandy because Colombo and Kandy are different areas of authorised practice.
disagreements.verifier_position: The corpus supports the rule but not the geography: nothing in the Notaries Ordinance as held here defines the judicial zones, so the step from 'practising in Colombo' to 'not authorised in Kandy' rests on facts outside the corpus. The conclusion is very likely right, but a lawyer should confirm the zone boundaries as at April 2020.

lawyer_questions: Does rule 31(22), read with sections 3, 4 and 4A, bar a Colombo-warranted notary from attesting anywhere in the Kandy judicial zone as at April 2020, and were Colombo and Kandy separate judicial zones at that date? The whole 'he cannot travel to Kandy' limb turns on this and the corpus does not define the zones.

Was section 34 in its April 2020 form (before the substitution by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.17) an offence provision covering breach of rule 31(12), and at what fine level after the Increase of Fines Act No. 12 of 2005? The corpus holds only the post-2022 text.

Should the gold answer also flag the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance and the Partition Law, or is confining it to the Notaries Ordinance the right reading of a three-mark question that asks only about that Ordinance?
